subject: Different results running qtl2 on different machines

messages.author: 74bb2243bb8c3b1b
messages.subject: Different results running qtl2 on different machines
parts:
Hi Kurl

We are running a 4way mapping population with multiple sites in qtl2. We previously discussed how to convert the probability from qtl to qtl2. We stacked the probability of 750 individuals for 19 sites and calculate the kinship . We then run a QTL model with kinship and use site as a covariate. Right now we are running this only for one phenotype "BIOMASS"

out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)

This model runs perfectly in our local server but takes almost 25 GB of RAM in each core. To make it faster we tried to run it on TACC cluster and we ended up with output that has negative LOD scores. To fix this issue, right now we are running only with two sites and this is the summary of scan1 we got for two sites:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
 > summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :-349.15  
 1st Qu.:-156.77  
 Median : -91.95  
 Mean   :-106.54  
 3rd Qu.: -42.54  
 Max.   :   2.44  

But if I remove additive and interactive cov if looks normal:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
> summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :0.00426  
 1st Qu.:0.36295  
 Median :0.76280  
 Mean   :1.17617  
 3rd Qu.:1.56336  
 Max.   :7.75820  


What is your thoughts for this issue?

Thanks!

Best,
Taslima

On Thursday, September 26, 2019 at 12:12:23 PM UTC-5, taslima haque wrote:
Hi Kurl

We are running a 4way mapping population with multiple sites in qtl2. We previously discussed how to convert the probability from qtl to qtl2. We stacked the probability of 750 individuals for 19 sites and calculate the kinship . We then run a QTL model with kinship and use site as a covariate. Right now we are running this only for one phenotype "BIOMASS"

out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)

This model runs perfectly in our local server but takes almost 25 GB of RAM in each core. To make it faster we tried to run it on TACC cluster and we ended up with output that has negative LOD scores. To fix this issue, right now we are running only with two sites and this is the summary of scan1 we got for two sites:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
 > summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :-349.15  
 1st Qu.:-156.77  
 Median : -91.95  
 Mean   :-106.54  
 3rd Qu.: -42.54  
 Max.   :   2.44  

But if I remove additive and interactive cov if looks normal:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
> summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :0.00426  
 1st Qu.:0.36295  
 Median :0.76280  
 Mean   :1.17617  
 3rd Qu.:1.56336  
 Max.   :7.75820  


What is your thoughts for this issue?

Thanks!

Best,
Taslima

I can't think of an easy way to do this. All I can figure out is to do
is the source all of the R files in the package.

  1. download the source .tar.gz and uncompress it
  2. loop over all of the files in the R subdirectory, using source()
with each.

  qtl2_dir <- "~/Code/qtl2/R"
  for(file in list.files(qtl2_dir)) source( file.path(qtl2_dir, file) )

But before doing this, I think I'd try to spot-check the results. For
example, if you use fit1() to fit the QTL model at a single position, do
you get the same results as scan1() at that position?

karl

Right now we are running this only for one phenotype "BIOMASS"

out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)

This model runs perfectly in our local server but takes almost 25 GB of RAM in each core. To make it faster we tried to run it on TACC cluster and we ended up with output that has negative LOD scores. To fix this issue, right now we are running only with two sites and this is the summary of scan1 we got for two sites:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
 > summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :-349.15  
 1st Qu.:-156.77  
 Median : -91.95  
 Mean   :-106.54  
 3rd Qu.: -42.54  
 Max.   :   2.44  

But if I remove additive and interactive cov if looks normal:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
> summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS       
 Min.   :0.00426  
 1st Qu.:0.36295  
 Median :0.76280  
 Mean   :1.17617  
 3rd Qu.:1.56336  
 Max.   :7.75820  


What is your thoughts for this issue?

Thanks!

Best,
Taslima
